newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Nelson Hurst says outlook strong.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Nelson Hurst says outlook strong.

text.p: British marine insurance firm Nelson Hurst Plc is expected to shrugg off a poor performance of its hull and liability division and show overall strong results for the year on stronger returns from its cargo and overseas operations, chairman David Woodward said on Tuesday.
"One can't expect any fireworks from us but our performance for the year will be solid," Nelson's Woodward told Reuters in a telephone interview.
The company had earlier said that a poor performance of its hull and liability division and an exchange loss out of a stronger sterling was likely to hit profits of the group.
"The hull and liability division formed in August 1995....continues to experience poor operating results," the company said in a statement.
Nelson created the division last year by recruiting a team of brokers from the former J.A. Chapman & Co.
The statement triggered a fall in its share price, which declined to a low of 125 pence from an overnight close of 186.5p but it later recovered some lost ground to close at 146.5p.
He said Nelson had now taken over direct management of the hull and liability division from the former Chapman executives and reduced their number from 32 to eight.
He said this was because failure of the Chapman team to transfer business from its old clients was one main reason for its performance falling below expectations.

"We are now on a stronger platform and hopefully next year should be better," the chairman said. Woodward said it was still witnessing a strong performance from its cargo division and its overseas operations, especially in the Asia Pacififc region.
Nelson's overseas turnover had increased by 14 percent in the first half to June, 1996. Woodward said it would be "either comparable or better" in the second half, ending in December.
Woodward said Nelson's overall performance for 1996 would be "better than many brokers" in the marine insurance business, which has witnessed a continuous decline of premium rates in recent months.
Earlier, in the statement Nelson said it did not expect any change in its progressive dividend policy.
